title: SpaceX CRS-34 Dragon Cargo Mission Set for May 12 at 7:16 p.m. EDT — ~6,500 lbs of Science Experiments and Crew Supplies Bound for ISS
detail: NASA confirmed around May 7–8, 2026 that SpaceX's 34th Commercial Resupply Services mission (CRS-34) will launch no earlier than May 12, 2026 at 7:16 p.m. EDT (23:16 UTC) from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The Cargo Dragon spacecraft will carry approximately 6,500 pounds of cargo including critical science investigations: a microgravity simulator fidelity study evaluating terrestrial simulator accuracy, a wooden bone scaffold for osteoporosis treatment research, a charged-particle monitor to study power grid and satellite infrastructure impacts, and a planetary formation research experiment. Dragon is scheduled to autonomously dock to the Harmony module's forward port at approximately 9:50 a.m. EDT on May 14. A NASA prelaunch media teleconference was set for May 11 at 11:00 a.m. ET. CRS-34 will be SpaceX's 57th orbital mission of 2026 if it launches as planned, extending SpaceX's unbroken ISS resupply record under the CRS-2 contract. The mission will deploy from SLC-40, the same pad used for the majority of SpaceX's Starlink, commercial, and cargo missions — and the newly inaugurated LZ-40 adjacent landing pad completes the rapid-turnaround landing infrastructure suite at Cape Canaveral.

title: SpaceX IPO Retail Investor Access Guide Published; Bank of America Warns Simultaneous Mega-IPOs Could Mark Bull Market Peak
detail: Two significant financial analyses published around May 8, 2026 shaped the pre-IPO landscape ahead of SpaceX's expected Nasdaq debut. The Motley Fool published a retail investor access guide explaining three routes for individual investors to gain SpaceX exposure: direct share allocation (SpaceX has committed 30% of the public float to retail — three times the standard allocation), post-IPO S&P 500 index fund participation after near-certain inclusion (which would trigger an estimated $200B+ in forced passive buying), and indirect exposure through companies with significant Starlink revenue partnerships including T-Mobile. Bank of America analysts warned via CNBC (May 6, 2026) that SpaceX and Anthropic's simultaneous mega-IPOs in 2026 could be a significant market inflection point — drawing historical parallels to the wave of blockbuster technology IPOs in 2000 that preceded a multi-year bear market. BofA noted that the combined IPOs could absorb hundreds of billions in equity market liquidity. Despite the warnings, SpaceX's public S-1 registration statement remains on track for publication around May 18–22, 2026 (the window required for a June 8 roadshow start under SEC rules), with Nasdaq pricing and debut targeted June 18–30 at a ~$1.75 trillion valuation and $75 billion capital raise target. Kalshi prediction markets show 82-85% probability of IPO announcement by July 1.
